english.title: Exposure - intent to cause alarm, distress or humiliation
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally exposed your genitals intending that someone would see them and be caused alarm, distress or humiliation
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66(1)(a) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from 29th September 2026 following amendments made by section 113 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026. For the offence applying before this date, see H5816. The amendments widened the scope of section 66 so that, in addition to the alarm or distress the offence of exposure may be committed by those who expose their genitals with the intent to cause humiliation to those who may see them. An offence at section 66(1)(b) was created where a person exposes their genitals for the purpose of sexual gratification, intending that their genitals will be seen by another person, and is reckless as to whether that person will be caused alarm, distress or humiliation, see H102885 for the substantive offence and H102887 for the attempt.(ii) "Genitals" refers to male or female sexual organs.(iv) This offence, where the victim or intended victim was under 18 at the time of the offence, is listed as a child sex offence in paragraph 10 to Schedule 34A to the Criminal Justice Act 2003 for the purposes of disclosing information relating to convictions for such offences to members of the public under section 327A (Sarah’s law).(v) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act as follows -
(a) where the offender was under 18 years of age where he is or has been sentenced in respect of the offence to imprisonment for a term of at least 12 months;
(b) in any other case, the victim was under 18 or the offender in respect of the offence or finding, is or has been sentenced to a term of imprisonment, detained in a hospital, or made the subject of a community sentence of at least 12 months. (Sch 3 paragraph 33).

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment. This is a specified child sex offence; where this offence is aggravated by grooming and the victim or intended victim was under the age of 18, see section 70A of the Sentencing Act 2020.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
